name: Anti-authoritarianism
summary: Anti-authoritarianism opposes imposed, unaccountable and hierarchical authority, above all that of the state, and insists that any authority be freely accepted, open to challenge and limited to what is necessary. In its most developed form it is anarchism, which holds that no state has a legitimate claim to obedience and that society can be organised by voluntary association and mutual aid. Its usual commitments are equality before the law and strong civil liberties.
scope: The anarchist-rooted core of the family, based on Bakunin's 'What is Authority?', Malatesta's 'Anarchy' and the Stanford Encyclopedia's survey of philosophical anarchism. It leans toward the libertarian-socialist mainstream and treats market-anarchist, pacifist and post-anarchist strands as variants. Liberal and pragmatist anti-authoritarianism (such as Dewey's) is noted but not the basis, and economic questions are often low confidence because the label is about authority rather than a program.

keyFigures.name: Mikhail Bakunin
keyFigures.role: Anarchist thinker who distinguished freely accepted expertise from imposed authority

keyFigures.name: Errico Malatesta
keyFigures.role: Anarchist author of 'Anarchy', describing society organised without government

keyFigures.name: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon
keyFigures.role: Summarised the aim of anarchism as 'no more authority'

sources.title: Anti-authoritarianism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, strands, thinkers, civil-liberties commitments, critics such as Engels.

sources.title: Anarchism
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Legitimacy of the state, hierarchy, obedience, violence, property and civil disobedience.

sources.title: What is Authority?
sources.author: Mikhail Bakunin
sources.usedFor: Accepted versus rejected authority, rule by experts, legislatures, privilege and religion.

sources.title: Anarchy
sources.author: Errico Malatesta
sources.usedFor: Government as class instrument, majority rule, voluntary organisation, law, education.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not an anti-authoritarian doctrine as such; adherents favor mutual aid and free access to care, but dislike state provision, so mild support at most.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Statist wage-setting is not a core concern; libertarian-socialist strands prefer abolishing wage labour while others back any gain for workers, so adherents split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Anarchist strands see markets bound up with property and domination; Malatesta ties government to owning-class exploitation, though market anarchists dissent.

public-ownership.rationale: Anti-authoritarians distrust state ownership as concentrated hierarchical power; they prefer common or cooperative ownership run by those involved.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation presupposes a state they question; they oppose concentrated wealth but not through state coercion, so adherents split.

unions-good.rationale: Malatesta cites unions among free voluntary associations; self-organised labour bodies are favoured over rule from above.

property-fundamental.rationale: Proudhon saw property as a source of despotism and Malatesta ties it to political domination, though market-anarchist strands disagree.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Calling on the state to regulate conflicts with rejecting state authority, yet they oppose corporate power; adherents split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not a stated position; mutual aid supporters oppose letting need go unmet, but cutting state programs is not opposed on principle by those who distrust the state.

worker-ownership.rationale: Self-managed workplaces fit the rejection of hierarchy in economic life, which SEP lists among the hierarchies anarchists oppose.

surveillance-ok.rationale: State watching of subjects is an instrument of government power that anti-authoritarians resist; security justifications are the usual pretext for authority.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Opposition to coercive state control over personal conduct leads to freedom for adults to use drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: handing the state power to police speech runs against civil liberties emphasis, though many oppose bigotry on other grounds.

strong-leader.rationale: Opposition to concentrated unaccountable rule is the defining core; Bakunin rejects privileged authority and rule by a few.

state-harmful.rationale: Political anarchists hold the state has no legitimate authority; Bakunin held the state is inseparable from slavery.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: disarming people while the state keeps arms is distrusted, but anarchists are not united on guns.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and soldiers are listed by Malatesta as core instruments of government force; more power for them is the opposite of the position.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state coercion over consenting adults; views vary on whether sex work is exploitative.

decide-locally.rationale: Decentralised consensual organisation is the positive ideal in SEP, preferring local self-direction over central authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Kropotkin called prisons schools for crime; adherents reject punitive state coercion in favour of reform and addressing causes.

traditional-family.rationale: Anarchists accept family ties only when free of coercion and question hierarchy in gender and family; no uniform view.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred: they oppose state licensing of marriage altogether but back the freedom of same-sex couples; reading literally yields mild support.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from bodily autonomy and opposition to state control of private choices; the sources do not address it directly.

more-religion-public.rationale: Bakunin rejects religious authority over people and SEP lists religion among hierarchies anarchists oppose.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: SEP lists race among hierarchies of domination anarchists oppose, supporting active efforts to dismantle them, though not necessarily through the state.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from opposition to gender hierarchy; the sources do not take a position on the nature of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred: nationalism is tied to the state and hierarchy, but cultural preservation as such is not a stated concern.

gradual-change.rationale: Inferred: adherents treat institutions as illegitimate and do not defer to them, though some favour gradual cultural change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Borders are state enforcement of authority over people's movement, which anti-authoritarians oppose.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Supranational bodies add another layer of governmental authority, which they oppose as they oppose national states.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to tariffs as state interference clashes with distrust of market power and capitalism, so split.

nation-first.rationale: Malatesta and Bakunin frame domination as between people not nations; the state and national interest are not authorities adherents defer to.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: state military action is distrusted as an exercise of government force, though some support protecting people.

open-borders.rationale: Rejecting the state's authority over movement leads to open borders as the natural position.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed in sources; ecological anarchism opposes human domination of nature but growth limits are no core tenet.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: SEP notes opposition to human domination of nature, but drastic government action conflicts with distrust of the state.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No stated position; adherents divide between techno-optimists and primitivist critics.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not a topic the sources address, and adherents divide on it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Malatesta notes subjects may have only an appeal to arms against usurped power, and violence is accepted by some as reactive though pacifist strands dissent.

experts-over-public.rationale: Bakunin accepts expertise only as free consultation and rejects rule by scientific bodies.

central-planning.rationale: Central planning needs a coercive central authority; Bakunin rejects rule by academies and privileged bodies over life.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between market-friendly cooperative models and anticapitalist communism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not discussed; it requires a taxing state and so is generally unwelcome, but some individualists value it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Opposes inherited privilege but taxation relies on state authority, so adherents are split.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: provision by the state is distrusted, though many welcome the redistribution.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred: tariffs are state intervention that serves owners and national interest rather than workers.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of the economy is an exercise of governmental authority that anti-authoritarians reject.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Proudhon favoured small possession but others favour collective ownership; adherents split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Kropotkin's all-for-all communist strand supports this, but mutualists and individualists keep exchange.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Central banks are state institutions, but a market answer is only part of the tradition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages and prices embody imposed hierarchy rather than free agreement.

one-party-rule.rationale: Concentrated political rule by a single party is direct authoritarianism, the antithesis of the position.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule is a privilege-based hierarchy; Bakunin holds privilege corrupts and equality is the basis of liberty.

democracy-best.rationale: Malatesta and Bakunin reject representative democracy and majority voting as legitimate authority, though Dewey's strand accepts liberal democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Anarchists reject majority rule as legitimating, though unanimous direct democracy is the form Wolff allows and consensus is favoured, so split.

workers-councils.rationale: Self-organised councils fit the preferred model of delegation of work not power, though anarchists reject any ruling body.

right-to-secede.rationale: If no state has legitimate authority over people, they may leave or break away from it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Bakunin denies infallible or permanent authority and rejects privilege; equality is the condition of liberty.

political-violence-never.rationale: Goldman and Malatesta accept violence as reactive, but pacifist strands such as Tolstoy's reject it; the majority view allows it in defense.

war-builds-character.rationale: War is conducted by states and relies on obedience; inferred from the rejection of state domination.

separate-church-state.rationale: Bakunin rejects clerical government and divine authority, and opposes both church and state domination.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Bakunin rejects authority imposed by God or men, and religious command over law is imposed authority.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists defend this while communist anarchists reject private provision; SEP records the split.

military-superiority.rationale: Military power serves state domination, which anti-authoritarians oppose.

ethnic-nation.rationale: SEP lists race among hierarchies anarchists oppose; exclusionary ethnic states are domination.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Malatesta sees government as serving the property-owning class, supporting class analysis, but adherents do not all adopt Marxist history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Equality is the basic condition of liberty for Bakunin, but equal outcomes enforced by authority is contested.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from opposition to colonialism and support for local self-determination.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-colonial but reparations entail state transfer; sources are silent.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred: political unions create larger states and authorities.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Anarchists emphasise mutual aid; individualist strands dissent.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Subordinating the individual to community duty enforced by authority contradicts the priority of individual liberty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: SEP mentions anarchist opposition to human domination of nature.

limit-population.rationale: State-enforced limits are opposed; the topic is not addressed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Green and primitivist anarchists agree, communist and syndicalist ones do not.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No stated position, and adherents split.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from bodily autonomy against state restriction.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Handing more decisions to a remote system adds authority over people.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Protecting people against state surveillance and control fits the opposition to government power.

restore-past-order.rationale: Anti-authoritarians seek to dissolve hierarchies, not restore a past ones.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pragmatist strand agrees while principled anarchists reject judging by results alone.

direct-action.rationale: Anarchists reject parliaments and elections as legitimating authority; Ellul refuses to vote and Malatesta calls suffrage an illusion.

means-match-ends.rationale: SEP states that for pacifist anarchists means and ends must match, and the idea is central to the tradition.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Only primitivist anarchists hold this; most adherents do not.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Kropotkin and others favoured integrated work, but not universal.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Kropotkin's all-for-all communism is cited by SEP, though individualist strands disagree.

production-for-use.rationale: Communist and mutualist anarchists favour need-based production; market anarchists differ.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Malatesta calls property a means of exploitation tied to political domination.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anarchists reject any dictatorial state power; Engels is cited as a critic of this anti-authoritarianism.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range between voluntary collectives and individual farming.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not an established position of the sources.

taxation-theft.rationale: No duty to obey the state means compulsory taxation lacks justification, as Thoreau's tax resistance shows.

harm-principle.rationale: Restricting only harm to others fits the general demand that coercion be justified, though anarchists oppose even such state authority.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individual liberty is central but collective rights of communities are accepted by collectivists.

conscription.rationale: Compelling people into military service is core state coercion that anarchists reject.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Neither voting nor leaving is a legitimate check for them; adherents reject both as accepting the state.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred: it still treats the state as legitimate.

positive-liberty.rationale: Bakunin ties liberty to equality and the material conditions of recognising laws one's self; many support the claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Contradicts opposition to racial hierarchy and Bakunin's equality premise.

organic-representation.rationale: Malatesta distinguishes delegation of work from delegation of power; representation structures of community bodies are still rejected.

total-state.rationale: The antithesis of the position: the state directing every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: It is nationalist and authoritarian in character, opposite in spirit to anti-authoritarianism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule resting on personal oaths of loyalty is hierarchical, privileged authority.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labour to a lord is a clear form of domination.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Post-anarchists extend the rejection of authority to repressive forms of power, but this epistemic claim is not a stated tenet.

single-common-good.rationale: Bakunin rejects imposed unitary order; pluralism, but not a stated point.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Inferred: creating a state is opposed on anarchist grounds, though rights of people are not.

revive-national-language.rationale: State imposition of language is opposed, but cultural revival itself is accepted.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Opposes hierarchy in economic life, though by consensus rather than state-mandated votes.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split on public schooling.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The topic of state fiscal policy is not addressed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Anarchists accept political freedom needs economic equality, while market anarchists argue economic freedom; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred: any ruler is rejected, though moral example over punishment is gentler; Malatesta says even good rulers are corrupted.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-authoritarians favour self-determination but reject the state as the vehicle.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred; state force abroad is opposed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Bakunin accepts only authority recognised by one's own reason, but emotion is not rejected by all.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from opposition to borders and hierarchy among people.

class-collaboration.rationale: Malatesta sees government as the instrument of the owning class, so partnership is rejected.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Futurist idea unaddressed; sources do not support destroying culture.

dominated-front.rationale: The sources say nothing on blocs of dominated countries; anarchists oppose Western power but distrust state-led fronts, so adherents split.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Gender hierarchy is among those anarchists oppose; legally fixed roles are imposed authority.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred: state prohibition is opposed, although Proudhon's mutualism criticised interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Race hierarchy enforced by law is explicitly the domination opposed.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Malatesta describes government as a means of exploitation serving the class holding economic power.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred; not addressed, mildly negative given ecological strands.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Forced cultural conformity is imposed authority; conflicts with free association.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claim, not an anarchist position though elites are distrusted.

proportional-representation.rationale: Malatesta rejects all electoral systems, so no electoral reform is a priority.

national-mission.rationale: State missions to spread government are domination.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: SEP lists gender among hierarchies anarchists oppose.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Malatesta and Bakunin argue that power corrupts rulers and elected bodies become a privileged class.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: State control of reproduction is coercive authority.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred; they oppose state violence, though accountability through courts is not their method.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Even a minimal state is illegitimate for political anarchists, though minarchists would agree and anarcho-capitalists are a strand.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial hierarchy and state interference in private life are both opposed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality is the basic condition of liberty for Bakunin and equal treatment is a usual commitment.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist debate over socialist states, which anarchists do not frame this way, so no clear answer follows.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equality before law is valued but state codification is not.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: State ban on practices is opposed, but vegan strands exist.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Malatesta says government-directed instruction teaches acceptance of authority, and Bakunin opposes clerical power.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Anti-authoritarians say no state is legitimate, even with consent; Wolff allows only unanimous consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export targets are a state economic policy the sources never discuss, and nothing in the principles favours either side.

population-transfer.rationale: Expelling or pressuring a minority is the kind of coercive state domination anarchists reject, though the sources do not discuss population transfers.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Goldman and Malatesta accept violence as reactive, which implies initiating force is the wrong, though revolutionaries qualify it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Kropotkin's mutual aid thesis contradicts it.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Banning parties is state repression of association; though anarchists reject parties too.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anarchism is defined as opposition to domination and arbitrary authority; rule by no one.

separated-powers.rationale: Checks on power are better than none, but anarchists reject the state altogether.

vanguard-party.rationale: Anarchists reject disciplined parties leading the masses; Engels and Draper are the critics.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is state provision and tenant purchase is a policy the sources never address; adherents have no common view.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Law restricting labour action is state coercion against workers' free association.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Malatesta and Kropotkin trace poverty to social institutions, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Contradicts opposition to racial and ethnic hierarchy.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Anarchists reject offices; lottery rotation is sometimes favoured, others say it still gives authority.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Suspending civil liberties for emergencies is the essence of authoritarian power.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred: state price-fixing is another central authority.

party-controls-media.rationale: State control of information is authoritarian.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party command of the military is concentrated authority.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Anarchists reject representatives altogether; pay cap not their cause.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding discipline conflicts with the individual right to criticise authority that Bakunin insists on.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Adds governmental authority, though a federation of free groups is accepted; the EU itself is a state structure.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Malatesta rejects all governors, kings, presidents and ministers alike, who enforce military service, so it opposes concentrating command of the army in a head of state; the head-versus-legislature question itself is not addressed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Malatesta treats religious authority as a way of defending privilege, so hierarchical church government runs against the tradition, though the sources do not discuss bishops versus congregations.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anti-state view favours it, though the sources do not address it directly.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship is imposed authority over thought, in tension with strong civil liberties.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Entrenched rulers are the opposite of the position.

recall-officials.rationale: Better than no accountability, but anarchists reject officials entirely.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances are state structures; antimilitarism is typical.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; mandated ownership is state coercion.

people-in-arms.rationale: Replacing a professional army with citizens is closer to the anarchist view, but the sources are silent.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources do not rank rural against urban life, and adherents hold varied views on it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Bakunin warns against rule by the learned, but a claim about graduates' everyday awareness is not a tenet, so split.

death-penalty.rationale: State killing is the extreme of state power; Kropotkin rejected prisons and punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Supports the content but rejects state schooling.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religious dogma taught through authority is opposed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: State restriction of consenting adults is opposed, though some feminist anarchists dissent.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Hereditary privilege and state membership are rejected.

minority-language-support.rationale: Supports linguistic freedom but not state programmes.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Anarchists oppose general laws but not necessarily exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Opposes conformity of customs as well as state coercion.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debts held by states serve ruling class; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Domination is economic as well as political, as Malatesta describes.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Prefers none; anarchists reject framing constitutions via elected bodies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Restricting liberty for development is authoritarian.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Mutual aid favoured but not state-to-state aid.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Still gives a ruler; election does not legitimate authority.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A central bank is a state institution, so independence from elected governments does not bear on anarchist concerns; no stated view.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims are state claims; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Anarchist critique of property sits close to this, but only the state enforcement is rejected.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anarchists criticised the Soviet state as another authority replacing capitalists, as Engels debate suggests.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Government action on risk is a policy question the sources do not address, and adherents have mixed views on state-led regulation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Opposes clerical power, but also state power; split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Military force to keep people in a state is the coercion anarchists oppose.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy for a region inside a larger state is a constitutional design question; anarchists reject states but would welcome autonomy, so split.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sacral hereditary rule contradicts equality and rejects divine authority.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Rate structure of state taxation is not a concern for those who dispute the state's right to tax at all; no position.

character-from-environment.rationale: Kropotkin sees prisons as schools for crime, implying environment shapes people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Bakunin writes that a body given absolute sovereignty, even one made up of the most illustrious men, would infallibly end in corruption, and that people should obey only laws they themselves recognise.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion as a civilizational goal is not addressed by anti-authoritarian sources, and adherents are indifferent.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rule by the few and many are both rejected as government.

leader-cult.rationale: Honouring leaders as embodiments of the nation is the opposite of anti-authoritarianism.

equal-parenting.rationale: Court presumptions about custody are a legal matter the sources never address; no common view among adherents.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This is a Maoist-style thesis about party leaders restoring capitalism; anarchists share distrust of party elites but frame it differently.

land-redistribution.rationale: Opposition to property concentration; however anarchists dislike state seizure.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Bakunin rejects laws imposed by any outside will, divine or human, and Malatesta counts government-backed religious authority as one of the ways governments oppress people.

women-must-cover.rationale: Imposed law on bodies and clothing is authority; gender hierarchy opposed.

common-currency.rationale: Whether states share a currency is a state monetary question the sources do not address, so no stated view.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Self-governing minority institutions within a state are not discussed in the sources; adherents favour self-organisation but reject state frameworks.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The choice between emigrating and fighting for rights is not covered by the sources, and adherents have no shared answer.

ban-cartels.rationale: State anti-trust is state action; anti-capitalist sentiment.

no-bailouts.rationale: State aid to firms serves the owning class; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Malatesta rejects majority rule as justice, but courts are state too.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Opposes gender hierarchy, rejects governing bodies.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding treaty standards imply enforcing bodies above states, which adherents dislike, yet they favour the aims; no clear answer.

moral-incentives.rationale: The sources do not discuss incentives, though Malatesta expects common interest to motivate work once property is gone; adherents are split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Propaganda of the deed advocates exist but others disagree.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Bakunin says privilege corrupts and equality is the condition of liberty.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial rule is among hierarchies anarchists oppose.

patriotic-education.rationale: Malatesta says state-directed instruction teaches people to accept authority.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Opposes racial hierarchy but also institutional preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: State money creation is state power.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources do not say whether capitalism can avoid collapse, and adherents vary in their economic forecasts.

delink-world-market.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is not addressed by the sources; adherents disagree on trade and self-reliance.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist theory about workers in rich countries is not part of the sources and adherents have no common view.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Market anarchists agree; others reject discriminatory hierarchy.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Civil liberties valued but anarchists reject states and constitutions as authorities.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anarchist opposition to colonialism and imposed state boundaries suggests mild agreement, but the sources do not discuss treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rulers by election still rejected, though better than hereditary.

minority-veto.rationale: Wolff allows only unanimous consent and Malatesta rejects majority rule over minorities.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: They accept resistance, though not limited to unconstitutional rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Bakunin rejects legislatures as a privileged class.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: SEP notes opposition to human domination of nature.

animal-use-humane.rationale: SEP notes opposition to domination of nature, but adherents divide between vegan and welfarist positions on animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternalistic hierarchy is rejected; mutual aid replaces charity from above.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Ellul refuses to vote but anarchists also engage in direct action.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred; Malatesta says teaching serves authority.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Malatesta says moral sentiment is used to make people accept arrangements favouring the powerful.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not part of the sources; adherents oppose exploitation but have no unified view of global economic structure.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns communist parties directing each other, which anarchists reject as party hierarchy but do not frame as a question of roads.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is outside the sources, and adherents are split between mutual aid and self-reliance.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Opposes fascism strongly but rejects constitutions.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anarchists criticise both authoritarian regimes, including Marxist ones.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not an anarchist position; slavery is the extreme of domination.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is not addressed by the sources, and adherents do not share a view.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources do not address programmes for boys and men; anarchists oppose gender hierarchy but not attention to disadvantage, so split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources are silent on comparative services for domestic violence, so adherents have no shared position.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Anti-authoritarians reject imposing any state form but do not frame the question by civilization, so adherents split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Malatesta describes government as the policeman of the privileged and says military conquerors concentrate power and property, so an army guarding the political order is opposed by implication.

paid-care-work.rationale: Opposes wages system but recognises care work.

filial-duty.rationale: SEP says parental authority is legitimate only in limited cases.

office-by-exam.rationale: Offices still imply a ruling class; Bakunin rejects rule by experts.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Free association applies to marriage too.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Malatesta separates delegation of work from power; bound recallable delegates are the anarchist preference over representatives.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private accounts favour finance; not addressed.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Occupancy and use tenure is a common anarchist view.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Bakunin sees elected legislatures as a privileged political class, so parliamentary budget control is not endorsed, though it limits executive power.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Borders and state property are rejected.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Legal tests for discrimination in outcomes are not addressed; anarchists oppose racial hierarchy but also state legal machinery, so split.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred; anarchists generally critical of consumer capitalism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: State covert action; though anarchists may back insurgents against states.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Invading an allied state to keep it in line is imperial domination.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Anarchists reject a strengthening state under any justification, the point at issue in the Engels debate over authority.

corporate-influence.rationale: Malatesta describes government as serving the class holding economic power, so corporate sway over government is an instance of that.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: SEP reports that anarchists reject any principled duty to obey, leaving obedience to pragmatism or choice.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Adherents distrust state power over civil society, media and schools, and such restrictions give the state control over independent bodies. Inferred from the opposition to unaccountable state authority.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the view that reproduction is a private choice; state steering of family size through incentives is a form of imposed authority, though some adherents accept it as mild.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: a local authority limiting who may buy property is coercive authority over exchange between individuals, though communal land control appeals to some anarchists.

job-guarantee.rationale: Adherents favour work free of bosses but dislike state provision; a state employer of last resort splits them.

democratic-peace.rationale: Anarchists doubt that states, democratic or not, bring peace and see all states as war-making, yet liberal anti-authoritarians accept the thesis; adherents are split.

non-intervention.rationale: Adherents reject the state's authority over its own people, which cuts against absolute non-intervention, but they also distrust state interventions abroad; the family is split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalist and libertarian-socialist strands favour industrial unionism as a voluntary form of worker organisation, though the label itself is not about unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Anti-authoritarianism stresses equality before the law and strong civil liberties, so conspiracy claims against a minority are rejected.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Anarchist writers have long opposed state regulation of marriage and held that unions should be free agreements between individuals, in line with rejecting state-conferred status.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Accountability and challenge of authority require that those who hold power be open to scrutiny, which supports access to government records.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed by the label; some anarchist strands favour local self-sufficient communities while others accept wider exchange.

informal-organisation.rationale: Malatesta and others stress voluntary association and affinity-based groups, though many anarchists also build federations and unions.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Adherents deny the legitimacy of any state's claim to obedience, so neither national nor international authority is preferred; inferred from the opposition to state authority.

religious-nation.rationale: Bakunin attacks religion as an instrument of authority, and the tradition rejects the state and national identity as bases of legitimate authority.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Anarchist anti-authoritarianism rejects hierarchy and deference as illegitimate, between states as within them.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Mutual aid and pooling according to need are anarchist values, though adherents distrust state redistribution; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Anarchist communists such as Kropotkin kept personal possessions private while holding productive property in common; market-anarchist strands split, so low.

defeat-communism.rationale: The anarchist core opposes both Soviet-style states and crusades led by states; inferred, since the label is about authority rather than a foreign policy.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Adherents split between state-run public services, voluntary mutual-aid provision and market provision; the label does not decide it.

religion-illusion.rationale: Bakunin treats religion as a consolation of the oppressed and an authority to be abolished with social inequality.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anarchists split on capitalism as a stage; Marx's view is not an anti-authoritarian doctrine, and the sources do not address it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anarcha-feminist and libertarian-socialist strands link domination of women to class and property hierarchy; inferred from the family's anti-hierarchy core.

socialized-care.rationale: Communal provision appeals to libertarian socialists but state-provided services are an authority concern; adherents split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from the opposition to state imposition, which includes official language policy.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the consent principle, under which agreements bind the state and cannot be rewritten unilaterally by a party holding power.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Voluntary self-governing communities holding property in common are the classic anarchist model of social organisation.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-steered settlement is an exercise of coercive state power over minorities, which anti-authoritarianism opposes; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anarchists criticise both capitalism and authoritarian state communism and seek free association as a different course; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Anarchist-rooted thinkers reject claims of right based on lineage or tradition, but do not discuss land claims directly; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The family's strong civil-liberties and equality commitments leave no room for denial; inferred rather than stated.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The strand's civil-liberties commitments and rejection of state policing of private conduct oppose such laws.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Anti-authoritarianism defends civil liberties and free organisation, and Malatesta treats government as a class instrument.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Bakunin attacks religious authority and the family's civil-liberties commitments oppose punishing belief or speech.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anarchists reject rule by one people over another as domination, inferred from their general opposition to hierarchy.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; Bakunin rejects religious authority, so a religious duty cuts against it, though resisting invasion is accepted; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Bakunin rejects religious authority, so religious law cannot be the test of legitimacy, and no one holds a right to rule.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Malatesta and Bakunin stress voluntary organisation and people running their own affairs instead of leaving them to officials.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not a stated doctrine, but opposition to all hierarchies makes it natural for adherents; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; the strand's equality and liberty commitments suggest support; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; individual autonomy over one's life suggests support; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The label concerns authority rather than a left-right program, and adherents range from libertarian socialists to market anarchists.

alienated-labor.rationale: The libertarian-socialist mainstream makes this critique, but the label itself is not an economic programme; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; civil-liberties commitments oppose group prejudice, but this is inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Bakunin explicitly rejects divine authority as the model of illegitimate command.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents oppose state-imposed dress codes and religion in state alike, so views are split; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; the strand's equality-before-law and anti-privilege commitments suggest support; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Anarchist-rooted adherents dislike state regulation as much as laissez-faire, so this middle route is unattractive; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Anarchists regard standing armies as instruments of state coercion and favour voluntary defence, though pacifism is not universal.

rich-first.rationale: The strand rejects privilege and hierarchies of wealth and power; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to state power blocs suggests support, inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Bakunin's 'What is Authority?' accepts only authority that is freely accepted and open to challenge, which hereditary succession of office violates.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from mutualist and cooperative traditions within anarchism; Malatesta's text does not discuss banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from opposition to imposed authority and the libertarian-socialist leaning; no stated position.

property-franchise.rationale: Anarchism and anti-authoritarianism reject privilege and hierarchy, and a wealth qualification for voting is a clear case of it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred from anarcha-feminist and social-ecology strands that link hierarchy over women and over nature; not universal.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept; libertarian-socialist adherents may accept it but the label is indifferent.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the libertarian-socialist mainstream's critique of economic power over the means of communication.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Anarchists reject rulers altogether, so the statement's premise of governing rulers conflicts, although arbitrary decrees are condemned too.

racial-franchise.rationale: Equality before the law and civil liberties are usual commitments, so an ethnic franchise is rejected.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred from support for open, horizontal participation; the sources do not mention online tools.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from demands that authority be open to challenge and accountable.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Strong civil liberties and opposition to imposed authority make legal restrictions on marriage by religion unacceptable.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Equality and civil liberties as usual commitments imply rejecting boycotts targeting a minority.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not stated in the sources; inferred from the anarchist preference for direct, non-hierarchical decision-making, which sortition-based deliberation resembles.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from Bakunin's rejection of infallible authority and the insistence that any doctrine stay open to challenge, which applies to inherited religious rulings.

missingStatements.text: Authority is legitimate only when those subject to it can freely question it and withdraw from it.
missingStatements.rationale: Bakunin accepts expertise only as a free listener keeping the right to criticise and recognises no infallible authority.
missingStatements.declined: Restates the anarchist critique of authority already captured by state-harmful, freedom-as-non-domination and consent-of-governed (answered); no cleanly separate question.

missingStatements.text: People have no general moral duty to obey the law merely because it is the law.
missingStatements.rationale: SEP reports that anarchists reject any principled duty to obey, leaving obedience to pragmatism or choice.

notes: Adherents split most on economics (communist, mutualist and market anarchists), on violence (pacifist versus reactive-violence views) and on whether democracy can be legitimate (Dewey's pragmatist strand accepts liberal democracy). Many economic and social answers are low-confidence inferences.
